messages.author: bc1d848aa84f1efe
messages.subject: Csize for specimen average shape
parts:
Hi all,

I'm trying to regress individual asymmetry on Csize, but I'm not seeing Csize for each individual. I have two LM configurations for each specimen in my sample, but I'm only finding Csize for each configuration in the GPA. Does bilat.symmetry have Csize for each individual and I'm just missing it? Or is there another way to find Csize for each individual rather than each configuration in my sample as is found with the gpagen function?

All the best,
Ashly

messages.author: aab55242ff4da6c6
messages.subject: Re: [geomorph-r-package] Csize for specimen average shape
parts:
Hi Ashly,

If your analysis is for object symmetry, there is no Csize output, but you could just perform GPA with gpagen and you will have Csize as output for the each specimen's entire configuration.  If you analysis is for matching symmetry, You could either perform GPA separately (there is an example in the help file how to run bilat.syymetry on a gpagen object, in which case you have Csize already form the gpagen object) or you can extract Csize indirectly from the $procD.lm.size$data output of the bilat.symmetry object.  Keep in mind you will have two or more centroid sizes for each specimen, so you would have to contrive a way to summarize them.  

Because an arbitrary choice must be made for how to summarize multiple centroid sizes per specimen (for matching symmetry), providing a full-specimen centroid size as output would mean asserting an arbitrary choice as appropriate, which (in my opinion) exceeds the scope of the bilat.symmetry analysis, and good reason not to include any centroid size output, other than for the matching configuration replicates (which it does already).

Hope that helps!
Mike

messages.author: aab55242ff4da6c6
messages.subject: Re: [geomorph-r-package] Csize for specimen average shape
parts:
I did not know that MorphoJ attempts to provide one centroid size for replicated configurations. I assume that the program finds the mean of configurations, unless otherwise stated in the documentation. Taking either the mean or the sum — assuming each specimen’s configuration is replicated the same number of times — would have the same ANOVA outcome when regressing individual asymmetry versus size. 

In case it helps, the simplest way to do this in R, for a gpagen object called GPA and a vector of specimen names called id is:

CombCsize <- by(GPA$Csize, id, mean)

Or 

CombCsize <- by(GPA$Csize, id, sum)

You might also need to use as.vector to remove unneeded formatting before analysis. 

Cheers!
Mike

Sent from my iPhone
